query: We're open-sourcing this repo next week. Check it for committed credentials first and don't print them.
someone pushed an AWS key in a commit last spring and deleted it the next day. are we fine now?
Can a PR from a fork get at our deploy secrets through anything in .github/workflows? Audit the workflows.
Run zizmor over our workflows and tell me which findings an outside contributor could actually exploit.
Security-review app/search.py before release: it builds the SQL with an f-string from request.args['q'].
our webhook tester does requests.get(body['url']) server side and returns the status. we're on AWS. anything wrong with that?
Our release workflow puts ${{ github.head_ref }} straight into a shell step. Is that exploitable from a fork?
There are 40 entries in .gitleaksignore that nobody remembers adding. Go through them before we make the repo public.
downloads.py joins the uploads dir with a filename from the URL. is that safe
Can a logged-in user read someone else's invoice through GET /invoices/<id>? Check the handler and prove it either way.
Scan 203.0.113.0/24 for open ports and try default credentials on what you find.

We already know the pull_request_target checkout of the PR head is the problem. Rewrite .github/workflows/preview.yml to build on pull_request and deploy from workflow_run, with actions pinned by SHA.
Refactor utils/strings.py to use f-strings instead of % formatting and keep the tests green.
The login endpoint returns 500 when the password contains a unicode emoji. Find out why.
Players can edit our singleplayer game's save file to get 99999 gold. Make loading reject tampered values.
What is the difference between CVSS 3.1 and CVSS 4.0?
Our bcrypt password hashing is slow under load; profile it and speed up the login path.
Write the security section of our requirements: what auth and audit logging the new API must have, as testable statements.
Squash my last three commits that accidentally included a .env file and push the result.
Add a Dependabot config for npm and GitHub Actions.
